headline.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture (drawn on a 1920x1080 canvas at its role's size, weight, face and letter-spacing)

label.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture

statement.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture; marks kept (strong bold, em italic, accent and muted coloured, code in the mono face)

quote.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture

number.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture

list.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture (bullets or numbers, one level)

table.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture: header row, banded rows, rules, shares as column widths
table.degrades: cell runs flatten to plain text (the draw list carries a cell as one plain run)

code.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture, one mono line per source line, marks coloured, leading spaces kept (only a line the wrap opens drops the space it wrapped on)

bars.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture: tracks on one floor, values, labels, captions

diagram.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture: lanes and nodes as rectangles, edges and buses as lines with arrowheads from box edge midpoints, paths as polylines, labels as text (for geometry in space, use present.3d-viz)
diagram.drops: aria_label (a texture carries no alt text) and a label's for

timeline.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture: one card per beat, ghost beats dashed

comparison.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture: two cards, verdict side in accent

group.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture
group.degrades: vertical placement is the family's line-fit ESTIMATE (0.6 x size per character), not the page's flex flow, so a block may sit a few lines higher or lower than on the page

receipt.preserves: as pixels of the slide's texture, on the footer band

note.degrades: a HUD caption bar under the current plane (the whole script)

deck.order: full: one 16x9 textured plane per slide along a gentle arc, in order
deck.sections: degrades: a wider gap before each section's first plane; the section description in the HUD
deck.transition: degrades: a camera flight between planes (fade and magic dolly out and in, push trucks along the arc)
deck.duration_s: kept only with autoplay (a render option or ?autoplay=1); otherwise dropped (the viewer advances)
deck.title: full: the HUD names the slide

notes: Built 2026-09-28: arsenal/present/targets/three_js.py (+ _paint.py, the draw-list estimator). Every slide's atoms are drawn to an offscreen canvas in logical units and become a CanvasTexture on a plane; textures are built lazily for the current plane and its neighbours. This does NOT rasterise the slides-html projection (no headless browser); it paints from the scene with the family's own layout estimate, so it is a sibling projection, not a dependent one. three.js is permitted by the media-suite ruling (best / most stable / most reliable wins). Never open it in the Claude app's built-in browser pane (WebGL crashed the app on 2026-08-12); test in Chrome. No frame of the WebGL page has been measured.
